plan.contextChunk: This figure is part of a worked example asking to find the volume of the tetrahedron bounded by the coordinate planes and the plane z = 4 - 4x - 2y using a double integral. The figure contains two linked diagrams. Left: a 3D perspective showing the tetrahedron in xyz-space with vertices at (0, 0, 4), (1, 0, 0), and (0, 2, 0), bounded above by the plane z = 4 - 4x - 2y (labeled on the slanted face) with the base region R labeled. Right (inset): the 2D base region R in the xy-plane, a right triangle with vertices at (0, 0), (1, 0), and (0, 2), bounded by the x-axis, y-axis, and the line y = 2 - 2x; a red vertical strip illustrates the inner integration limits from y = 0 to y = 2 - 2x. An arrow connects the two diagrams. The figure establishes the correspondence between the 3D tetrahedron and the triangular base R over which the iterated double integral is set up.

elements: 3D tetrahedron with vertices at origin, (1,0,0), (0,2,0), (0,0,4)
slanted triangular face of the plane z = 4 - 4x - 2y (translucent teal)
base triangle R in the xy-plane (vertices (0,0), (1,0), (0,2))
x-axis arrow pointing down-left with tick label 1 at (1,0,0)
y-axis arrow pointing right with tick label 2 at (0,2,0)
z-axis arrow pointing up with tick label 4 at (0,0,4)
teal dots at the three intercepts (1,0,0), (0,2,0), (0,0,4)
label 'z = 4 - 4x - 2y' beside the slanted face
label 'R' on the base triangle
vertical cross-section slice on the tetrahedron at the strip's x (highlighted, red-edged lamina from base up to the plane)
2D inset panel: xy-axes, right triangle R with vertices (0,0), (1,0), (0,2), hypotenuse line y = 2 - 2x in teal, teal dots at (0,2) and (1,0), labels 'y = 2 - 2x', 'R', tick labels 0, 1, 2
red vertical integration strip in the 2D panel from y=0 up to y=2-2x at the current x

interactions.label: Strip position x
interactions.teaches: Dragging the strip sweeps x across R: the red strip in the 2D triangle and the matching vertical cross-section of the tetrahedron move together, showing that the inner integral over y (0 to 2-2x) is one slice of the volume and the outer integral sweeps x from 0 to 1
Rotating the tetrahedron reveals that the slanted face is a single flat plane over the triangular base R, so volume = height z integrated over R

interactions.label: Focus
interactions.teaches: Switching between the 3D solid and the 2D region traces how the tetrahedron projects straight down onto the triangle R — the domain of the double integral is the shadow of the solid on the xy-plane

demo_steps.title: The solid and its shadow
demo_steps.narration: The tetrahedron sits over the triangular region R. Focus on the 2D region to see R alone: a right triangle bounded by the axes and y = 2 - 2x.

demo_steps.title: One inner-integration strip
demo_steps.narration: At fixed x the red strip runs from y = 0 up to y = 2 - 2x; in 3D the matching lamina rises from the base to the plane z = 4 - 4x - 2y. That strip is the inner integral.

demo_steps.title: Sweep the outer integral
demo_steps.narration: Slide x from 0 to 1: the strip shortens as the hypotenuse descends, and the highlighted slice sweeps across the whole tetrahedron — accumulating the volume ∫₀¹∫₀^(2-2x) (4-4x-2y) dy dx.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: World units match coordinates: tetrahedron vertices exactly (0,0,0), (1,0,0), (0,2,0), (0,0,4); slanted face is the plane z = 4 - 4x - 2y over base triangle R. Layout as in source: x-axis recedes down-left from origin, y-axis runs screen-right, z-axis straight up. Slanted face and base R translucent teal (#7fc9c4, ~0.45 opacity) with thin teal edges; intercept dots teal #2aabb0; axes black with arrowheads; labels black serif italic. Cross-section slice at strip x: a thin vertical lamina spanning y in [0, 2-2x], z in [0, 4-4x-2y], filled warm red #d94f4f at 0.5 opacity with solid red outline; a red vertical line from (x,0,0) to (x, 2-2x, 0) links it to the base. 2D inset panel drawn as a flat XY plot on the right of the scene (or overlay): x from 0 to 1, y from 0 to 2, triangle filled same teal, hypotenuse teal line thickness ~3, red strip a vertical bar from y=0 to y=2-2x at the slider's x (~0.55 initially, i.e. strip top at y≈0.9 as in source). Curved tan arrow from 3D panel to 2D panel may be omitted or drawn as a simple arc in 'Both' mode.
interactionPlan.notes: In 'Both' mode render the 3D scene left and the 2D inset as a fixed overlay on the right (orthographic sprite or second viewport); '3D solid' and '2D region R' modes zoom the camera to fill the frame with one panel. Orbit applies to the 3D panel only and is disabled while focused on the 2D region. Update strip, lamina, and connecting red line reactively each slider change; cross-section height at the strip's right edge must satisfy z = 4 - 4x - 2y exactly.

interactions.label: Strip position x
interactions.teaches: Dragging the strip sweeps x across R: the red strip in the 2D triangle and the matching vertical cross-section of the tetrahedron move together, showing that the inner integral over y (0 to 2-2x) is one slice of the volume and the outer integral sweeps x from 0 to 1
Rotating the tetrahedron reveals that the slanted face is a single flat plane over the triangular base R, so volume = height z integrated over R

interactions.label: Focus
interactions.teaches: Switching between the 3D solid and the 2D region traces how the tetrahedron projects straight down onto the triangle R — the domain of the double integral is the shadow of the solid on the xy-plane

demo_steps.title: The solid and its shadow
demo_steps.narration: The tetrahedron sits over the triangular region R. Focus on the 2D region to see R alone: a right triangle bounded by the axes and y = 2 - 2x.

demo_steps.title: One inner-integration strip
demo_steps.narration: At fixed x the red strip runs from y = 0 up to y = 2 - 2x; in 3D the matching lamina rises from the base to the plane z = 4 - 4x - 2y. That strip is the inner integral.

demo_steps.title: Sweep the outer integral
demo_steps.narration: Slide x from 0 to 1: the strip shortens as the hypotenuse descends, and the highlighted slice sweeps across the whole tetrahedron — accumulating the volume ∫₀¹∫₀^(2-2x) (4-4x-2y) dy dx.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: World units match coordinates: tetrahedron vertices exactly (0,0,0), (1,0,0), (0,2,0), (0,0,4); slanted face is the plane z = 4 - 4x - 2y over base triangle R. Layout as in source: x-axis recedes down-left from origin, y-axis runs screen-right, z-axis straight up. Slanted face and base R translucent teal (#7fc9c4, ~0.45 opacity) with thin teal edges; intercept dots teal #2aabb0; axes black with arrowheads; labels black serif italic. Cross-section slice at strip x: a thin vertical lamina spanning y in [0, 2-2x], z in [0, 4-4x-2y], filled warm red #d94f4f at 0.5 opacity with solid red outline; a red vertical line from (x,0,0) to (x, 2-2x, 0) links it to the base. 2D inset panel drawn as a flat XY plot on the right of the scene (or overlay): x from 0 to 1, y from 0 to 2, triangle filled same teal, hypotenuse teal line thickness ~3, red strip a vertical bar from y=0 to y=2-2x at the slider's x (~0.55 initially, i.e. strip top at y≈0.9 as in source). Curved tan arrow from 3D panel to 2D panel may be omitted or drawn as a simple arc in 'Both' mode.
interactionPlan.notes: In 'Both' mode render the 3D scene left and the 2D inset as a fixed overlay on the right (orthographic sprite or second viewport); '3D solid' and '2D region R' modes zoom the camera to fill the frame with one panel. Orbit applies to the 3D panel only and is disabled while focused on the 2D region. Update strip, lamina, and connecting red line reactively each slider change; cross-section height at the strip's right edge must satisfy z = 4 - 4x - 2y exactly.

plan.authoredPrompt: This figure is part of a worked example asking to find the volume of the tetrahedron bounded by the coordinate planes and the plane z = 4 - 4x - 2y using a double integral. The figure contains two linked diagrams. Left: a 3D perspective showing the tetrahedron in xyz-space with vertices at (0, 0, 4), (1, 0, 0), and (0, 2, 0), bounded above by the plane z = 4 - 4x - 2y (labeled on the slanted face) with the base region R labeled. Right (inset): the 2D base region R in the xy-plane, a right triangle with vertices at (0, 0), (1, 0), and (0, 2), bounded by the x-axis, y-axis, and the line y = 2 - 2x; a red vertical strip illustrates the inner integration limits from y = 0 to y = 2 - 2x. An arrow connects the two diagrams. The figure establishes the correspondence between the 3D tetrahedron and the triangular base R over which the iterated double integral is set up.
plan.authoredInteractions:
- Drag the red vertical integration strip in the 2D base panel and watch the corresponding cross-section highlight on the 3D plane z=4-4x-2y update in real time
- Rotate the 3D tetrahedron to view the triangular plane from different angles
- Toggle between the 3D and 2D panels to trace how the triangular integration region R projects onto the xy-plane
plan.sourcePath: Anton, Bivens, and Davis. Calculus, 10th Edition, Figure 14.2.10
